mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST QoQ change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically distinguishable from a flat market at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5 percentage points over three months signals easing monetary policy alongside falling inflation, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS change < -0.5% AND CPIAUCSL change < -0.5% over 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth above 0.5%) combined with a concurrent rise in retail sales (proxied by RSAFS growth above 0.7%) signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% AND RSAFS monthly change > 0.7%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.2 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly change > 0.2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 800 thousand units for four consecutive months signals a prolonged housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction-related equities and broader consumer confidence, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.
